questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Keeping accents on capital letters
questions.learningObjective: Identify whether the capital keeps its accent
questions.stem: Item 0001 asks whether the capital letter in a printed French word keeps its accent mark.

options.text: The capital keeps the accent in modern French print.
The capital keeps the accent only in handwriting.
The capital always drops the accent in print.
The accent moves to the following vowel.
options.misconception: misplaces the accent onto another vowel

questions.explanation: Modern French keeps accents on capitals in print. The tempting idea that capitals drop accents is outdated and wrong.
questions.hint: Check current spelling rules for capitals.

provenance.author: bank-team-french

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: The ligature oe written as one sign
questions.learningObjective: Recognise when oe is written as one sign

stimulus.body: French spelling keeps accents on capitals in print. The ligature oe may be written as one sign. The circumflex distinguishes words that sound alike.

questions.stem: Item 0002 asks when the ligature oe is written as a single sign in French.

options.text: The ligature oe is never written as one sign.
options.misconception: denies the existence of the ligature

options.text: The ligature oe is written as one sign in standard print.
The ligature oe is written as one sign in set words.
options.misconception: assumes a fixed list never changes

options.text: The ligature oe is written as one sign only in names.
options.misconception: restricts the ligature to proper names

questions.explanation: Standard French print uses the ligature oe in set words. Restricting it to names or denying it is wrong.
questions.hint: Look for the ligature in printed words.

options.text: The circumflex distinguishes homophones in spelling.
The circumflex changes the pronunciation always.

options.text: The circumflex marks a nasal vowel.

questions.explanation: The circumflex often distinguishes homophones in spelling. It does not always change sound or mark nasals.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: quatre-vingts before a noun and before a numeral

stimulus.body: French numbers keep special plural forms. Quatre-vingts changes before a noun or numeral. The plural mark on cent also changes in context.

options.text: Quatre-vingts always keeps the final s.
Quatre-vingts drops the s before a noun.
Quatre-vingts never has a final s.
Quatre-vingts drops the s before a numeral.

questions.explanation: Quatre-vingts drops the s before a numeral. Keeping it always or dropping before a noun is wrong.

questions.explanation: The colon takes a narrow no-break space before it. Commas and periods do not.
